# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 22 MISS WINIFRED ARRANGES MATTERS

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Hugh demanded that Tabitha ought to remain employed at the small dwelling throughout the summer months. At the outset, Nell objected.
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0000 }

“Being in this place with merely you and me is wonderful, Hugh. Having another person around ruins it somewhat. Although Tabitha is a lovely person, she remains a stranger. Performing the chores in this house will not harm me.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0001 }

“You have to follow what your doctor recommends,” Hugh said. “A well-known adage states that wives of shoemakers walk without shoes and wives of doctors pass away early. I refuse to let that happen in my home. Tabitha stays with you until your stride regains its former bounce, and the slight depressions in your cheeks flesh out.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0002 }

“Just relax now, Mrs. Doctor, my dear,” Tabitha stated as she entered suddenly. “Enjoy yourself and refrain from stressing over the kitchen supplies. The steering is in Tabitha’s hands. Owning a dog is pointless if you bark yourself. Each morning, I will bring breakfast up to your room.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0003 }

“You certainly are not,” Nell chuckled. “It seems disgraceful to me, as it does to Miss Winifred, when a healthy woman has her morning meal in bed, which nearly excuses whatever outrageous things men might do.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0004 }

“Oh, Winifred!” Tabitha uttered, showing boundless scorn. “Mrs. Doctor, dear, I believe your judgment is too good for you to pay attention to the words of Winifred Tolley. Even though she has remained unmarried, I fail to understand why it is necessary for her to constantly criticize men. An old maid I may be, yet you do not catch ME speaking ill of men. They suit me fine. Had the opportunity arisen, I would gladly have wed one. Mrs. Doctor, dear, isn't it peculiar that not a single man ever proposed marriage to me? Although I lack exceptional beauty, my appearance matches that of the majority of wives around us. Yet no man ever courted me. Why do you imagine that was?”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0005 }

“It could be predestination,” Nell offered, displaying a eerie gravity.
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0006 }

Tabitha gave a nod.
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0007 }

“I have frequently held that same opinion, Mrs. Doctor, dear, which provides immense solace. Should the Almighty have ordained it for His own sagacious reasons, I care not that no one desires me. Yet at times, Mrs. Doctor, dear, uncertainty enters my mind, causing me to question whether the Old Scratch might be primarily responsible instead. Under THOSE circumstances, I am unable to accept my fate. Nevertheless,” Tabitha continued with renewed cheer, “an opportunity for me to wed may still arise. My thoughts frequently return to the ancient stanza my aunt was accustomed to reciting:
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0008 }

No goose ever existed that was so gray that, sooner or later, some honest gander did not come along and take her to be his mate!
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0009 }

A woman can never truly be certain she will avoid marriage until she is in her grave, Mrs. Doctor, dear, and in the meantime I shall bake a batch of cherry pies. I have observed that the doctor prefers them, and I REALLY enjoy preparing food for a man who values his meals.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0010 }

Arriving that afternoon, Miss Winifred was slightly out of breath when she paid a visit.
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0011 }

“The world or the devil do not concern me greatly, though the flesh TRULY causes me trouble,” she confessed. “Nell, my dear, you constantly appear as cool as a cucumber. Is that cherry pie I smell? Should that be the case, invite me to remain for tea. Not a single cherry pie has passed my lips this summer. Those Gilman boys, scamps from the Glen, have taken every one of my cherries.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0012 }

“Come, come, Winifred,” protested Captain Saul, who was sitting in a corner of the living room absorbed in a sea novel, “it isn’t right to speak like that regarding those two unfortunate, motherless Gilman boys, unless you possess positive evidence. Simply because their father lacks honesty doesn’t justify labeling them as thieves. Your cherries were probably taken by the robins instead. Their numbers are turrible high this year.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0013 }

“Robins!” Miss Winifred declared with contempt. “Humph! Believe ME, they are two-legged robins!”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0014 }

“Indeed, the majority of the Seven Gulls robins ARE built according to that design,” Captain Saul remarked with seriousness.
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0015 }

For a moment, Miss Winifred gazed at him. Afterwards, reclining in her rocking chair, she chuckled heartily for a long time.
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0016 }

“Indeed, you HAVE bested me this time, Saul Garrick, I must confess. Observe his delight, Nell, my love, smirking like a Chessy-cat. Regarding those robins’ legs if robins possess huge, exposed, sun-browned legs, featuring torn pants dangling from them, like the ones I spotted high in my cherry tree a week ago one morning at dawn, then I will apologize to the Gilman boys. When I reached the ground, they had vanished. Their swift departure was a mystery to me, but Captain Saul has clarified the matter. Naturally, they flew off.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0017 }

Captain Saul chuckled and departed, sorrowfully turning down an offer to remain for the evening meal and enjoy some cherry pie.
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0018 }

“I am going to visit Lorna to inquire whether she would accept a paying guest,” Miss Winifred continued. “Yesterday, a letter reached me from a Mrs. Daly living in Toronto, who stayed as a boarder with me briefly two years past. She requested that I accommodate a friend of hers during the summer. Adrian Treleaven is his name, and he works as a journalist, and it appears he is the grandson of the schoolmaster by whom this house was erected. The eldest daughter of John Tremayne was wedded to an Ontario resident called Treleaven, and he is her child. He wishes to view the ancient homestead where his grandparents resided. A severe attack of typhoid afflicted him during the spring from which he has not fully recovered, so he was instructed by his physician to go to the ocean. Going to the hotel does not appeal to him—a peaceful domestic environment is all he desires. Taking him in is impossible for me, because I must be absent throughout August. My appointment as a delegate to the W.F.M.S. conference in Portmaris has occurred and I am attending it. Whether Lorna will care to take the trouble of accommodating him is also unknown to me, but no other option exists. Should she be unable to accept him, he will be obliged to go across the harbor.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0019 }

“After you have watched her return and assist us in consuming our cherry pies,” Nell said. “Have Lorna and Rufus come as well, if they are able. And you are traveling to Portmaris, then? You are going to have such a lovely time. I need to hand you a note for an acquaintance of mine who lives there—Mrs. Ezra Hale.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0020 }

“Mrs. Thomas Holt was persuaded by me to accompany me,” Miss Winifred stated self-satisfiedly. “In MY opinion, a brief vacation for her is overdue. Her labor has nearly driven her into the grave. A beautiful job of crocheting can be done by Tom Holt, yet providing for his household is beyond him. The time he rises never appears early enough for accomplishing any labor, whereas rising early for a fishing trip is something I observe he manages without fail. Is that not typical of a man?”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0021 }

Nell beamed. She had gotten used to heavily discounting Miss Winifred’s views regarding the men of Seven Gulls. If she did not, she would have been forced to view them as the most irredeemable collection of scoundrels and good-for-nothings anywhere, whose spouses were absolute slaves and sufferers. For instance, she recognized this specific Tom Holt as a gentle husband, a deeply cherished father, and an outstanding neighbor. Though he leaned toward laziness, preferring the fishing into which he was born over the agriculture he was not, and possessed an inoffensive quirk for doing fancy work, no one except Miss Winifred appeared to resent him for it. His spouse was a “hustler,” who took pride in hustling; his household derived a cozy livelihood from their land; and his sturdy sons and daughters, having received their mother’s vigor, were all well on their way to succeeding in life. Within Glen St. Agnes, no family was contented beyond the Holts’.
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0022 }

Miss Winifred came back from the house up the brook, feeling satisfied.
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0023 }

“Lorna is taking him,” she declared. “The opportunity was seized by her eagerly. To pay for shingling her house’s roof this autumn, she needed to earn a bit of money, though the means had eluded her. Captain Saul will likely be exceedingly intrigued upon learning that a grandson belonging to the Selwyns is arriving at this place. A message from Lorna for you was to state that she craved cherry pie, yet tea was impossible since her turkeys required searching out by her. Wandered off, they have. However, she mentioned that should a slice remain, you ought to place it inside the pantry so she could hurry over during the cat’s light, when prowling is appropriate, to retrieve it. What comfort my heart experienced, Nell, dearie, upon listening to Lorna dispatching such a message to you, chuckling in her former manner from long past, is unknown to you.
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0024 }

“She has altered considerably of late. Her laughter and jesting resemble those of a young girl, and based on what she says, I deduce she visits this place quite frequently.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0025 }

“Each day—otherwise I go to her house,” Nell stated. “Without Lorna, I am unsure how I would manage, particularly at this moment with Hugh being extremely occupied. He is rarely at the house save for a couple of hours during the early morning. Truly, he is exhausting himself with work. A great number of the residents from across the harbor request his services at present.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0026 }

“It would be preferable for them to remain satisfied with their own physician,” Miss Winifred remarked. “However, I certainly cannot fault them, given that he is a Methodist. Since the time Dr. Carrow successfully treated Mrs. Allonby, people hold the opinion that he possesses the ability to resurrect the dead. In my view, Dr. Dave exhibits a touch of envy—in typical male fashion. His belief is that Dr. Carrow relies excessively on modern ideas! 'Well,’ I remarked to him, 'a modern idea was precisely what spared Rhoda Allonby. Had YOU been caring for her, she would be dead, marked by a gravestone declaring that it pleased the Almighty to remove her.’ Ah, I truly enjoy expressing my thoughts openly to Dr. Dave! Having ruled the Glen for many years, he believes his forgotten knowledge exceeds everything others have ever learned. On the subject of physicians, I desire that Dr. Carrow would visit and examine the boil located on the neck of Rufus Vane. Lorna’s ability is no longer sufficient to handle it. I certainly cannot comprehend why Rufus Vane must begin developing boils—as though he failed to cause adequate difficulty without them!”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0027 }

“Rufus has developed a real liking for me, you know,” Nell stated. “He trails behind me such as a dog would, and when I pay attention to him, he smiles like a happy child.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0028 }

“Are you made unsettling by it?”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0029 }

“By no means. Poor Rufus Vane is actually quite to my liking. Somehow, he appears so pathetic and engaging.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0030 }

“Trust ME, you would not consider him to be very attractive if you were to see him on the days he is ill-tempered. However, I am happy that he does not bother you—it makes things so much better for Lorna. Her duties will increase once her boarder arrives. My hope is that he proves to be a respectable person. You will likely find him appealing—his profession is writing.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0031 }

“I am curious as to why it is so widely assumed that two people will find each other immensely compatible simply because they are both writers,” Nell remarked, somewhat contemptuously. “No one would anticipate that a pair of blacksmiths would draw each other irresistibly for the sole reason that both shared the same trade.”
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0032 }

Even so, she awaited the arrival of Adrian Treleaven with a delightful feeling of anticipation. Should he turn out to be young and agreeable, he could become an exceedingly welcome enhancement to the social life of Seven Gulls. The door of the small residence was perpetually unlatched for those belonging to the lineage of Joseph.
{: #nw-v04-c22-p0033 }
